title: Hazard screening and contaminated water
audience: Supervisors, coordinators and trained cleaners who may be asked to triage, refer or document mould-related work in homes, rentals and commercial buildings, under an approved plan. Not a qualification or authority to remediate, demolish, or certify any building or room.
learningOutcomes: Identify flood or sewage water and suspected asbestos or lead in a described scene, and stop work.
Isolate the area without disturbing material.
Record the hazards and the escalation in the risk register.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers screening and escalation. It does not authorise disturbing suspected asbestos or lead, handling contaminated water, or sewage clean-up, and it does not set out how to clean or dry a flood-affected home.

instruction.heading: Contaminated water changes the job
instruction.body: Water from floods, and sewage, must be treated as contaminated, and the job changes once it is present. The WA guideline has an appendix on managing mould risk after flooding. It says mould can grow within 24 to 48 hours in flood-affected homes, and that homes should be cleaned and dried as soon as possible. It advises removing wet items, floor coverings and wet plasterboard, discarding soft materials with mould growth, and not using diesel equipment indoors. Those are remediation steps that depend on the flood assessment and the approved plan, so a screening worker stops, isolates and refers them rather than starting them.

instruction.heading: Suspected asbestos and lead
instruction.body: Older building materials may contain asbestos or lead, and disturbing them can release those hazards. A ceiling that collapses to reveal suspicious old insulation under sewage-affected plasterboard presents both hazards together. Stop work, isolate the area and escalate. Presumed asbestos is not disturbed by an ordinary cleaner, and any sampling or removal is carried out by a competent person and, where the law requires, a licensed one. The Victorian asbestos guidance says a limited amount of asbestos removal can be done without a licence, sets limits for non-friable material and contaminated dust, does not list friable material among those exemptions, and advises considering a licensed removalist where obligations may not be met. A cleaner does not rely on any allowance.

procedure: Stop work where flood or sewage water is present, or where older materials may be disturbed.
Isolate the area, and keep occupants and unauthorised people out.
Do not disturb suspected asbestos or lead material, and record its location.
Escalate to a competent person and, where the law requires, a licensed person.
Record the hazards, the isolation and the escalation in the risk register.
Restart only on a written scope from the competent supervisor.

workedExamples.situation: A ceiling collapses to reveal suspicious old insulation under sewage-affected plasterboard.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop work and isolate the area. Do not disturb the insulation. Treat the water as contaminated, escalate to a competent and, where required, licensed person, and record the isolation in the risk register.

workedExamples.situation: After a flood, a cleaner is asked to remove the wet carpet and plasterboard before any assessment.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the request within routine cleaning?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Removing wet floor coverings and plasterboard is a remediation step that depends on the flood assessment and the approved plan. Stop, record the request and refer it.

equipmentAndPpe: Risk register for recording hazards, isolation and escalation.
Barrier tape and signage for the isolated area.
Training-only simulated risk register. No real contaminated water or building material is handled in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Disturbing old insulation or plasterboard under sewage-affected material without assessment.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, isolate and escalate for asbestos and lead assessment by a competent and, where required, licensed person.

commonErrors.error: Treating flood water as an ordinary wet surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat flood or sewage water as contaminated until a competent assessment says otherwise.

commonErrors.error: Using diesel equipment indoors to dry a home.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the approved drying plan. The WA guideline advises against diesel equipment indoors.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Asbestos and lead disturbance and sewage remediation are restricted to competent and, where the law requires, licensed people. This lesson does not grant any licence.
The Victorian asbestos guidance was read on 2026-11-03. Asbestos rules in other states and territories were not checked for this lesson.

summary: Flood or sewage water changes the job.
For suspected asbestos or lead: stop, isolate, escalate.
Do not disturb presumed hazardous materials.
Restart only on a written, competent decision.

knowledgeChecks.question: A ceiling collapses to reveal old insulation under sewage-affected plasterboard. What is first?
options: Remove the insulation to see its condition.
Dry the plasterboard quickly with fans.
Stop work, isolate the area and escalate, without disturbing the insulation.

knowledgeChecks.question: According to the WA guideline, how soon can mould grow in flood-affected homes?
Which statement about suspected asbestos is correct?
options: An ordinary cleaner may remove it with gloves.
It is not disturbed by an ordinary cleaner, and sampling or removal is done by a competent and, where required, licensed person.
It can be bagged and put in general waste.

WA Department of Health, Guidelines for managing mould and dampness, April 2024 edition, Appendix E, read 2026-11-03 through a page-summary tool.

Asbestos Victoria, Unlicensed removal, https://www.asbestos.vic.gov.au/builders-and-trades/asbestos-removalists/unlicensed-asbestos-removal, page shows an 'Updated' label and no date, read 2026-11-03 through a page-summary tool.

DISCREPANCY for owner review: the HR04 draft states a one-hour-in-seven-days allowance, a 10-square-metre figure and Class A and Class B licence classes. The page read on 2026-11-03 showed a 10 square metre area limit for non-friable material and a 10-minute total time limit for contaminated dust, and did not show the seven-day allowance or licence classes. These are not used in this lesson.
UNCONFIRMED: lead disturbance rules, sewage remediation licensing and asbestos rules in other states and territories were not checked for this lesson.

officialReferences.title: Guidelines for managing mould and dampness: related public health risks in buildings (WA Department of Health)
officialReferences.pageDate: April 2024 (version control table); publication code ENV-0014702 MAY'24; no separate last-updated date shown
officialReferences.covers: Read through a page-summary tool on 2026-11-03 (PDF, Environmental Health Directorate, WA Department of Health). Section 1.4 sets out a general public health duty, a workplace duty and a residential tenancies duty. Section 2.1 names people with existing respiratory, immunocompromising and allergic conditions, and infants, children and older people. Section 3.2.2 says porous items are often not economically salvageable and must be thrown out. Section 3.3 says the source must be located to address the cause and prevent recurrence. Section 3.4.1 defines simple contamination as new, isolated and visible, no greater than one square metre, with easily identified causes, and its footnote calls the one-square-metre size arbitrary. Section 3.4.2 defines complex contamination as larger than one square metre or found in multiple rooms or places. Section 3.5 states there are no defined quantitative or qualitative exposure thresholds for mould or dampness. Section 4.1 lists containment, drying and source repair as principles. Section 4.2.2 advises scrubbing hard surfaces with soapy water, avoiding dry brushing, cleaning at least 30 to 50 cm beyond the visible mould, removing or discarding porous items that cannot be adequately cleaned, stating that mould is not considered hazardous waste, and not painting, sealing or covering surfaces until dry. Section 4.3 recommends a site-specific plan with professionals for complex contamination, isolation with heavy grade plastic and negative pressure, and evacuation of occupants. Section 4.4 lists no recurrence within two to four weeks after remediation as an indicator of success, recommends the evaluation be done by a different entity, and states there are no legal requirements for a post-remediation assessment. Appendix B recommends a P2 or N95 respirator and says PAPRs should be used for complex remediation. Appendix E says mould can grow within 24 to 48 hours in flood-affected homes.

officialReferences.title: Unlicensed removal (Asbestos Victoria, Victorian Government)
officialReferences.pageDate: no date shown (page shows an 'Updated' label only)
officialReferences.covers: Read through a page-summary tool on 2026-11-03. The page says an employer or self-employed person can conduct a limited amount of asbestos removal work without a licence. It sets limits for removing non-friable asbestos-containing material and for removing asbestos-contaminated dust. It does not list friable asbestos among those exemptions. It advises considering a licensed asbestos removalist where obligations may not be met. The limit figures on the page are not used in this lesson. Publisher: Asbestos Victoria (Victorian Government).

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to remediate, demolish, disturb building materials, handle contaminated water or waste, or certify that a building, room or occupant area is safe or free of mould or pathogens. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Restricted or high-exposure remediation is carried out only by an appropriately qualified and competent professional under an approved plan, and some related work, including asbestos and lead disturbance and certain waste handling, is restricted to licensed or specially authorised people. The owner, manager, tenant or contract may define what work is permitted, but where the contract covers only routine cleaning, that is the limit of the task. Where the controlling authority or the competent supervisor is not identified, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: the hazards are unknown or changing; the work is destructive or hazardous and outside the authorised scope; exposure is uncontrolled or the building is unsafe to occupy; supervision, equipment or permissions are insufficient; flood, sewage, asbestos or lead may be present; a worker's PPE or respirator readiness has not been verified; a client asks for a clearance or pathogen-free statement; or a waste route is unauthorised. A stop-work decision is correct. Record it and restart only after the competent supervisor has confirmed the scope in writing.
